exposure: vaginal bleeding not related to PCB
outcome: delivery prior to 37 weeks of gestation
cohort: The participants were all singleton deliveries from pregnant women between 24 and 34 weeks of gestation referred due to vaginal bleeding, along with a comparison group of pregnancies without vaginal bleeding, from two tertiary medical centers over an 11-year period.
finding: Third-trimester post-coital bleeding (PCB) is a significant risk factor for preterm delivery, with rates similar to other causes of third-trimester bleeding but notably higher than the general population without bleeding.
gest_age: Exposure measured between 24 and 34 weeks of gestation; primary outcome was delivery prior to 37 weeks of gestation.
